feedback.problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={e}^{3{x}^{2}-3}$ at the point where $x=-1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={e}^{u},\,u=3{x}^{2}-3.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{u}\cdot 6x \\  & =6x\cdot {e}^{u} \\  & =6x{e}^{3{x}^{2}-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-1} & ={6x{e}^{3{x}^{2}-3}|}_{x=-1} \\  & =6(-1){e}^{3(-1)^{2}-3} \\  & =-6\cdot {e}^{0} \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$
